# Emirati Air Quality Index (UAE)

Code `ae_eaqi` · version 2023 · scale: index 0–500 · method: segments

## Sources

- [National Center of Meteorology, Guideline for calculating the Emirati Air Quality Index (EAQI), 2023, Table 3](https://airquality.ncm.gov.ae/resources/pdf/aqi-quickguide-en-2023.pdf), accessed 2026-10-21

## Categories

| Level | Category | Index | Colour | Health message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Good | 0–50 | `#00E400` | No risk for the population. |
| 2 | Moderate | 51–100 | `#FFFF00` | Acceptable for the majority of the population. |
| 3 | Unhealthy for sensitive groups | 101–150 | `#FF7E00` | Sensitive individuals should avoid exposure. |
| 4 | Unhealthy | 151–200 | `#FF0000` | A greater proportion of the public may be affected. |
| 5 | Very unhealthy | 201–300 | `#8F3F97` | Everyone may experience health effects. |
| 6 | Hazardous | 301–500 | `#7E0023` | The entire population is expected to be affected. |

## Rules

- US-EPA (2018) method: SI = (I_hi - I_lo)/(BP_hi - BP_lo) x (C - BP_lo) + I_lo, using truncated concentrations. O3, SO2, NO2, PM10 are truncated to 1 ug; CO to 0.1 mg; PM2.5 to 0.1 ug.
- Each sub-index is rounded half-up to an integer. EAQI = max sub-index.
- O3: compute both the 1-h and 8-h sub-indices and take the larger. A 1-h value below the national standard (200 ug) is not used. When the 8-h value exceeds 392, only 1-h is used.
- SO2: when the 1-h value exceeds 797, the 24-h rolling mean is used.
- Rolling means need at least 6 of 8 or 18 of 24 valid hours. With fewer: the sub-index is null if all hours are below the national standard, otherwise the maximum hourly value is used.
- Hourly values above the validation thresholds (CO 150.4 mg; SO2 1750.4; NO2 2000.4; O3 1000.4; PM 2500.0 ug) are treated as invalid.

## Implementation notes and source discrepancies

- Two cases the guideline does not specify, decided by us: (1) above the top breakpoint but below the validation threshold (e.g. PM10 600-2500), we extrapolate along the top band and flag beyond_scale. (2) 1-h SO2 > 797 while the 24-h mean is < 798: sub-index = 200, following the US-EPA 2018 Technical Assistance Document that the guideline builds on.
- Table 2 and Table 3 of the guideline differ slightly (e.g. CO 'Good' is 0-5 in Table 2 and 0.0-5.4 in Table 3). The guideline says to compute with Table 3, so we do.
- The worked O3 example mentions breakpoints '125 and 169' but computes with 121/167. Our test asserts the published result: 135.485 ug gives 116.
